## Data

```{r data}
library(tidyverse)
netflix_titles <- read_csv("netflix_titles.csv")
head(netflix_titles)
```

## Step 3: Inferential Statistics

The research question for this part of the project is, how accurately can we predict the genre of a movie based on its director, release year, and rating?

```{r test_train_split}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(forcats)
library(caret)
library(nnet)
library(car)
library(ggplot2)

netflix_movies <- netflix_titles %>% filter(type == "Movie")
netflix_movies <- netflix_movies %>% filter(listed_in %in% c('Children & Family Movies', 'Dramas', 'Horror Movies') )
netflix_movies <- netflix_movies %>% select(director, release_year, rating, listed_in)
netflix_movies <- netflix_movies %>% drop_na()
netflix_movies <- netflix_movies %>% mutate(listed_in = factor(listed_in), rating = factor(rating), director = factor(director)) %>% droplevels()

train_indices <- createDataPartition(netflix_movies$listed_in,p = 0.80,list = FALSE)[, 1]

netflix_movies_train <- netflix_movies[train_indices, ] %>% droplevels()
netflix_movies_test <- netflix_movies[-train_indices, ] %>% droplevels()

# simplify directors by combinging rare ones
netflix_movies_train$director <- fct_lump_min(netflix_movies_train$director, min = 5, other_level = "Other")
train_directors <- levels(netflix_movies_train$director)
test_directors <- as.character(netflix_movies_test$director)
test_directors[!test_directors %in% train_directors] <- "Other"
netflix_movies_test$director <- factor(test_directors,levels = train_directors)
```

```{r check-data}
ggplot(netflix_movies_train, aes(x = listed_in)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "blue")

ggplot(netflix_movies_test, aes(x = listed_in)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "red")
```

```{r train-logistic-model}
model <- multinom(formula = listed_in ~ release_year + rating + director, data = netflix_movies_train)
summary(model)
```

```{r multicollinearity}
vif_model <- lm(release_year ~ rating + director, data = netflix_movies_train)
vif(vif_model)
```

```{r accuracy}
train_pred <- predict(model,newdata = netflix_movies_train,type = "class")
test_pred <- predict(model,newdata = netflix_movies_test,type = "class")

train_cm <- confusionMatrix(factor(train_pred, levels = levels(netflix_movies_train$listed_in)), netflix_movies_train$listed_in)

test_cm <- confusionMatrix(factor(test_pred, levels = levels(netflix_movies_train$listed_in)), factor(netflix_movies_test$listed_in, levels = levels(netflix_movies_train$listed_in)))

train_cm
test_cm

cat("Training accuracy:", round(train_cm$overall["Accuracy"], 3), "\n")
cat("Testing accuracy:", round(test_cm$overall["Accuracy"], 3), "\n")
```

```{r confusion-matrix}
confusion_df <- as.data.frame(test_cm$table)

ggplot(
  confusion_df,
  aes(x = Prediction, y = Reference, fill = Freq)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Test Set Confusion Matrix",
    x = "Predicted Genre",
    y = "Actual Genre",
    fill = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
